Alex: heads-up — we just saw a regression in multi-GPU inference p99 on the dedicated fleet after the kernel heuristics change. p99 up ~2.3x for some TP+PP configs when traffic crosses PCIe-only links :frowning:
Marta: ugh. which models / configs? any obvious correlation with NVLink vs PCIe?
Alex: mostly 8xA100 TP2+PP1 with model shards that end up spread across a rack boundary (no NVLink). Local NVLink runs look fine. The timeline matches the kernel selector change that prefers conv-fused kernels for short seqs.
Jing: can you paste the profiling? curious if it's compute or all-reduce stall.
Alex: pasted below from nsys aggregate (trimmed):
```
nsys stats summary
operation                 avg_ms   p50_ms   p99_ms   wait_for_allreduce_ms
kernel_forward_conv       0.9      0.8      1.5     0
allreduce_fp16            0.7      0.6      12.2    9.8
kv_fetch_local            0.3      0.2      0.9     0
kv_fetch_remote           0.8      0.7      4.3     3.4
```
Alex: note allreduce p99 spike and remote KV fetch p99 — looks like comm/compute overlap is failing and KV cache miss rate climbs when shards are cross-node.
Sam: are the allreduces synchronous barrier-style or using NCCL async+streams? Should be async but maybe our kernel choice serialized streams.
Tori: the kernel selector change added an aggressive single-stream path for fused conv kernels, which looks great NVLink-local but kills overlap with NCCL on PCIe. it binds to stream0 and waits on it.
Marta: can we flip kernel selector back for crossnode topologies only? or at least use multi-stream fallback when link_bandwidth < threshold.
Jing: also we saw KV cache thrash: remote shard fetch rate doubled because batch packing changed. batching heuristic now packs more microbatches into a single global batch which increases working set and eviction pressure on KV cache on hosts that are remote.
Alex: repro script attached (ran on stage): `./perf/run_crossnode_batchprobe.sh --nodes 2 --micro 8 --seq 2048` — results stable on NVLink, bad on PCIe.
Sam: quick experiments I ran: forcing kernel=fallback (old path) reduces p99 from 250ms -> 95ms on PCIe case, and allreduce p99 goes down to ~2ms. suggests it's interplay, not raw NIC.
Tori: action idea: make kernel selector topology-aware. heuristics: prefer single-stream fused path only when intra_node_nvlink=1 for all shard pairs OR when expected_allreduce_bytes < X. otherwise pick multi-stream or split-kernel variant.
Marta: +1. also need a short-term config ramp: rollback heuristic on all dedicated pools with mixed fabric. we should add an opt-in flag for customers but default to safe.
Jing: on KV side: change batching heuristic to cap combined working set per host. simple approach: estimate per-shard KV footprint = embed_size * num_tokens_inflight and avoid packing microbatches that push remote eviction above 70%.
Alex: I ran a KV-prefetch trace: eviction rate goes from 8% -> 41% crossing node. will dump logs to the thread.
deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-18T14:02Z started: rollout/rollback/heuristic-v0.9 -> canary group eng-runtime-stage
Sam: propose short-term tasks: 1) config rollback for heuristic-v0.9 on dedicated PCIe pools (Sam) 2) implement topology-aware kernel selector gate (Tori) 3) adjust batching cap heuristic and add eviction metric to trace (Jing) 4) add e2e perf test covering cross-node TP+PP (Alex)
Tori: I'll sketch selector changes today; we need a small perf matrix for NVLink vs PCIe vs EFA to tune thresholds.
Marta: Jing, can you add a regression alert that fires when allreduce p99 > 5x baseline or kv_remote_eviction_rate > 20% on a pool? want automated detection.
Jing: will add alert and a dashboard panel. also starting a perf run now to capture full counters for the bad config.
Alex: thanks. can we aim to rollback the aggressive kernel path from prod pools by EOD if alerts reproduce?
Marta: let's do that. please post deploy links and checklist in this thread. :thumbsup:
Alex: posted logs + nsys captures to S3: s3://redwood-perf/1856783456/nsystraces.tar.gz
Sam: will take the rollback. assigning PR revert to me: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/PR-1287
Tori: starting selector PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/PR-1291 (WIP)
Marta: good. follow-ups: once rollback is in, run the cross-node e2e and confirm kv cache eviction and allreduce p99 back to baseline, then we can iterate on the topology-aware selector and batching caps.
Alex: thanks everyone. ping me for infra creds if you need the stage nodes. :eyes:
